method: Source-level reading only of the read-only Lean tree at clone 8937a8f (no lake/lean run, nothing written under the tree). Started from the arc-6 agent-5 pointers (file+line) for the five PARTIAL statements, read each cited declaration from source, then searched the tree for any declaration matching the paper clause the pointer does not cover (grep on paper labels 'Theorem 3.1', 'Proposition 9.9', '(3.6)', 'Lemma 4.4', '(4.17)', '(4.19)', 'Corollary 7.3', 'Lemma 9.7', 'Definition 3.3', 'q_big', and on content: rpow with 2*h error terms, X_in, rescal*, Lipschitz, 'chosen before'/'precede'). Manuscript clause text taken from writeup/data/arc6/ledger/merged.json (primary shard entries). Import-path question answered by computing the transitive import closure of NavierStokes/ComparatorSolution.lean from the modules' own `import` lines (Python over the .lean files; 580 modules, matching arc 6's count) and checking membership of every pointer module; the declaration-level dependency graph (which would need lean/lake) was NOT computed. The exported theorems were read at ComparatorSolution.lean:16-27 -> ComparatorR3Theorem.lean:36 / ComparatorTheorem.lean:48 -> R3ActualCandidate.lean:18 / ActualCandidateAssembly.lean:1183 (selected_candidate) -> selected_witness (1177) -> Witness (1121).

paper_clauses: Constants 0<h<1/100, q_*>0, 0<X_a<X_ext<inf and smooth (u,p) on Omega_*={tau>0, q<q_*} exist such that:
(i) u = curl A + B e_theta, A and B e_theta smooth in Cartesian coordinates at the axis, u exactly divergence-free.

(ii) every Cartesian space-time derivative of A, B e_theta, p is uniformly bounded on compact spatial subsets with c<=q<=c'<q_* up to the one-sided boundary tau=0, with limits compatible under differentiation.
(iii-a) |d_x^alpha d_t^b R(u,p)| <= C q^N on 0<=X<=X_1 as q->0, for every alpha,b,N,X_1 (3.4).
(iii-b) for X>=X_ext: residual identically zero, A=0, B=K(r,tau)=r^{-1-2h}H_ext(tau/r^2), p=-int_r^inf K^2/rho, K solves the radial swirl heat equation (3.5).
(iv) for some X_in in (0,X_a), e_0>0: u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau),0,0,1-tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0+O(tau^{2h})) as tau->0 (3.6).

lean.what_it_states: structure SmallParameters (h j : ℝ) : Prop where h_pos : 0 < h; h_le : h ≤ 1 / 1000; j_pos : 0 < j; j_le : j ≤ 1 / 1000. The actual profile's h carries this via NominalProfile.AxisStage.small (NominalProfile.lean:64) — stronger than the paper's 0<h<1/100.

missing_or_different: NOT STATED: no Lean declaration asserts the existence of a local pair (u,p) on Omega_* = {tau>0, q<q_*} with items (i)-(iv) as a package. The construction goes from finite stages (StageEstimates + extensions) directly to ProblemStatement.candidateStatement (periodic, time-activated, spatially localized fields), folding Theorem 3.1, Prop 9.9 and Section 10 together (MixedCandidateAssembly.lean:130, GermCandidateAssembly.lean:164, ActualCandidateAssembly.lean:1121).

(iv) MISSING: the rate u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau),0,0,1-tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0 + O(tau^{2h})) is absent in every form. What exists is the exact leading formula for the axial component at the origin x=0 (BaseResidual.lean:62; MixedAxisPreservation.lean:507), which is a different observable (u_z at r=0, not u_theta at X=X_in), and it is consumed only as Tendsto ‖u(t,0)‖ atTop. The only q^(2h)-type error bounds found (AllBandBaseJets.lean:97-98: ‖blownJet m (swirlError a h C d) (q, w)‖ ≤ B * q ^ (2 * h)) concern the base's normalized swirl/axial errors on an inner box, not the evaluation on the path (sqrt(2 X_in tau),0,0). grep for X_in / innerRadius found no counterpart.

(iii-a) DIFFERENT: (3.4) is uniform on {0 ≤ X ≤ X_1} for each finite X_1; Lean's AllJetsFlat / VanishingJointJets is along the filter 𝓝[openPast 1] (1,0) (a spacetime neighbourhood of the singular point), i.e. joint flatness at (1,0), not a bound parameterised by X_1. Flatness away from the origin is instead subsumed by the one-sided smooth extensions (AwayExtensions) and the boundary-limit theorems.

(iii-b) RESTRUCTURED: X ≥ X_ext is realised as w ∉ ActualPolarCoverage.active (X outside Icc activeLeft activeRight); higher stages vanish there (ExteriorStages) and the stage-0 base equals the explicit heat fields on cartesianExterior. Not checked: whether the paper's X_ext and Lean's activeRight coincide (numerically irrelevant for the exported statement).

(ii) RESTRUCTURED/STRONGER: replaced by existence of smooth one-sided extensions across t=1 at every x ≠ 0 (OneSidedExtension) plus derived compatible boundary tensors (exists_smooth_compatible_limits). The paper's restriction c ≤ q ≤ c' has no counterpart because the extension is pointwise-local.

(i) RESTRUCTURED: u = curl(cut potential sum) + direct angular sum; axis smoothness of B e_theta is by construction (AngularData.vanishes: the scalar vanishes for radius < inner), not stated as a Cartesian-smoothness lemma; exact divergence-freeness is via SolenoidalDiagonal (curl after cutoff) and CandidateProperties.divergence_free.

Constants: h is bounded by h ≤ 1/1000 (SmallParameters.h_le), which implies the paper's h < 1/100; q_* is ActualCandidateConstruction.qbig B N0 = ChartScales.Q (firstBand B N0) (line 155), fixed once.
statements.how_checked: All pointer modules (ActualCandidateAssembly, MixedCandidateAssembly, DiagonalResidual, BaseExterior, ModulatedExterior, JointResidualLimits, BaseResidual, BlowupImplication, MixedAxisPreservation) are in the 580-module transitive import closure of ComparatorSolution.lean (computed from import lines). The exported statements (ComparatorSolution.lean:16-27) assert only the comparator's breakdown propositions; their proofs consume, of Theorem 3.1's content, exactly CandidateProperties/R3CompactCandidate.Properties (smoothness on [0,1)×space, periodicity or compact support, zero datum, exact NS at viscosity one, SpeedUnboundedAtOne) — see ComparatorTheorem.lean:25-54 and ComparatorR3Theorem.lean:19-43. Declaration-level dependency tracing was not performed (needs lean).

paper_clauses: alpha << beta (alpha ≥ 0, beta > 0) means alpha/beta is required to be sufficiently small, the allowed size depending on all data already fixed.
In a chain of constants, choices proceed from right to left; small reciprocals specify large parameters.
For expressions depending on profile variables the smallness is uniform on the stated domain and ensured by those parameter choices.

lean.what_it_states: noncomputable def heightCap (core : OutgoingSchedule.Parameters) (extra : ℝ) : ℝ := min (core.lam / 4) (min extra (min (1 / 1000) (min (1 / 4) (1 / (1 + TerminalCone.releaseBudget core))))) — docstring: 'chosen before the terminal exponent h'. missing_or_different: There is no Lean definition of a relation '<<' nor of an order-of-choices convention; grep for '<<' (outside shift operators), 'right to left', 'smallness order' finds only docstrings (e.g. 'chosen before', 'precede' in ~30 files).

The convention is realised implicitly: every place the paper writes a chain a << b << ... is a Lean theorem whose quantifier alternation ∃M ∀Λ≥M ∃C₀ ∀C≥C₀ ∃r ∀δ<r ... fixes the order, or an explicit numeric cap (1/1000, 1/120, lam/4).
Nothing is missing that could be a theorem: a notational convention has no propositional content to formalize.
statements.how_checked: NaturalAxisData, ReferenceBounds, OutgoingProfile, ScheduledProfileChoice are in the import closure. A convention cannot weaken a kernel-checked statement; the order of choices is enforced by Lean's binder scoping in each existence theorem, which is strictly more rigid than the paper's convention.

paper_clauses: (i) If (U_1,E_1)=(U_2,E_2) for X ≥ X_h and Delta m(X_h,eta)=0 (five cumulative integrals M,I,J,S,C_p agree at X_h), then m_1=m_2 and Pi_i, V_{0,i}, Q_{s,i}, N_{s,i}, p_{s,i}, a_i, b_{s,i}, T_{0,i} agree for all X ≥ X_h, eta ∈ [-1,1].

(ii) (4.17): ||Delta(Q_s,N_s,p_s)||_k ≤ C_k (||Delta(U,E)||_{k+1} + ||Delta m||_{k+1}) on R=[X_0,X_1]×[-1,1] with E_i ≥ e_min, C_k depending only on k,h,X_0,X_1,e_min, the C^{k+1} norm of Pi_ax and a common C^{k+1} bound; no radial derivative of a difference occurs.

Remark (4.19): under the rescaling X = rho x, hat H = H/sqrt(rho), hat m = (M/rho, I/rho^{3/2}, J/rho^{3/2}, S/rho, C_p), hat p_s = p_s/rho the same estimate holds on a fixed x-rectangle with a constant independent of rho.

gate_answer: Per statement, at source (clone 8937a8f): Theorem 3.1 = MISSING-CLAUSE — items (i)-(iii) are present in restructured form (cut-potential curl + direct angular sum with axis smoothness by support, one-sided smooth extensions across t=1 at every x≠0, AllJetsFlat/VanishingJointJets residual at (1,0) plus vanishing of all corrections outside the active X-annulus and an exact heat base on cartesianExterior), but item (iv), the swirl rate u_theta(sqrt(2X_in tau),0,0,1-tau)=tau^{-A}(e_0+O(tau^{2h})), is absent in every form: Lean has only the exact leading axial formula at the origin, ((1-t)^(-A) * W.axis.j) • e_2 (MixedAxisPreservation.lean:507, BaseResidual.lean:62), used solely as Tendsto atTop → SpeedUnboundedAtOne, and no local-field theorem on Omega_* is ever stated. Definition 3.3 = NOT-A-THEOREM-IN-LEAN (the '<<' convention is realised by quantifier alternation and numeric caps such as SmallParameters.h_le : h ≤ 1/1000). Lemma 4.4 = WEAKER — part (i) holds for f,U,M,Pi via the equal-after lemmas (ModulatedExterior.lean:28-115) and the stronger exterior heat identities; part (ii) exists only at output order k=0 for the two stocks Q_s,N_s (ModulatedStockBounds.profile_stocks_lipschitz, line 225) and in the special observation form (RepairConeBounds.lean:1205); no C^k, k≥1 version, no p_s difference bound, no rescaling remark (4.19). Corollary 7.3 and Lemma 9.7 = NOT-A-THEOREM-IN-LEAN — realised by construction: one qbig B N0 = ChartScales.Q (firstBand B N0) (ActualCandidateConstruction.lean:155), a constant cycle-parameter sequence (line 37), one geometry (ActualCycleGeometry), StageEstimates on one physicalSublevel h qbig with stage/order-dependent constants only, and derivative inputs consumed through FiniteJetBound m (AllJetBound is unused outside JetBounds.lean). Import path: every pointer module of all five statements lies in the 580-module transitive import closure of ComparatorSolution.lean, but the answer to 'is the kernel-checked theorem weaker than a paper reader would assume because of a missing piece' is NO for all five: the exported theorems assert exactly the comparator's breakdown propositions, whose proofs consume only CandidateProperties / R3CompactCandidate.Properties (smoothness, periodicity or compact support, zero datum, exact NS at viscosity one, SpeedUnboundedAtOne); none of the missing pieces (the (3.6) rate, the general (4.17)/(4.19) estimate, the stated-domain lemmas) is asserted by, or needed for, those statements. The one reader-visible gap is at statement scope, not hidden inside the proof: the formalization certifies breakdown/unbounded speed, not the paper's blow-up rate, as arc 6 already recorded for Theorem 1.1. This is a source-level (module-closure) determination; declaration-level dependency tracing needs lean and was not done.

what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing here is a kernel check; no Lean was run. Verdicts are about the presence/absence of statements in source, not about the validity of proofs.

'NO' on the import-path question means: no missing clause makes the exported theorem weaker than its own printed statement. It does not mean the exported statement equals the paper's Theorem 1.1 — the blow-up rate is out of scope of the Lean statement (a statement-level fact, visible to any reader of ComparatorSolution.lean).
Membership in the import closure is necessary, not sufficient, for a declaration to be used by the exported proof; unused declarations inside imported modules are not distinguished at source.

The identification of Lean objects with paper objects (e.g. profileStockOne/Two with Q_s/N_s; active annulus with [X_a,X_ext]; W.axis.j with e_0) rests on docstrings and content matching, not on a formal correspondence.
Tier 2 is never a proof; nothing here moves any wall.
